Messages.Author: Sylvain Gogel
Messages.Body:
about Form of mist; one of the errata don't seems clear ...
"The superior form cannot be used by the acting vampire unless he needs the
stealth [RTR 19970630] "

When do we consider the acting vampire need the stealth since we don't know
if defending players want to block or not ?

Tzimiscelord, Primogen, Paris

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Sylvain Gogel wrote:
>
> about Form of mist; one of the errata don't seems clear ...
> "The superior form cannot be used by the acting vampire unless he needs the
> stealth [RTR 19970630] "
>
> When do we consider the acting vampire need the stealth since we don't know
> if defending players want to block or not ?

He needs stealth if there is a current blocking minion with intercept
greater than or equal to his current stealth. [6.2.2.2]

So superior FoM can only be played by an acting vampire if:
1) He's in combat with a blocking minion
2) The blocking minion's intercept >= his stealth (typical, since he's in combat)
3) He hasn't played Form of Mist at superior already this action

Messages.Author: Pat Ricochet
Messages.Body:
>> So superior FoM can only be played by an acting vampire if:
>> 1) He's in combat with a blocking minion
>> 2) The blocking minion's intercept >= his stealth (typical, since he's in
> combat)
>> 3) He hasn't played Form of Mist at superior already this action
>
> When will 2) ever not be the case?

Well, if it's a stealthed, then unblocked Bum's Rush, the acting minion
will be in combat with more stealth then the opposing minion has intercept.
However, that's not "the blocking minion," and so it covered in 1).
I guess you'd need something weird, like a Fleshcraft that reduces
intercept. (Eyecraft?) Even then, it's even more complicated. If I rush go
to Arson a hunting ground, and get blocked and play "Eyecraft" (maybe there
is a combat effect that reduces intercept, just not off the top of my head)
I might then want to press and play superior Form of Mist, which would seem
fair, really. I mean, I got blocked, and the card is to let me go on with
my Arson, but this says I can't play it, because I already have too much
stealth. I guess I could play Shadow Body, though, since it doesn't add
stealth. (don't ask me what vampire has all these abilities, I'm making up
cards to answer the question as I go, anyway)
I guess I set out to answer the question, but have to say I'm just as
confused. I can see how "The opposing minion" may have less intercept then
they do stealth, but not "the blocking minion."

--

Well, as you surmise, 1) implies 2) almost always.
But besides the examples given by others in which 1) doesn't hold
and therefore 2) can be trivially avoided, there are some ways to
do it:

Vamp A bleeds.
Vamp B, with Mr. Winthrop, blocks.
Vamp A gets +2 stealth from Lost in Crowds.
Vamp B gets +1 intercept from KRCG News Radio.
Action is blocked (1)
Vamp A plays Weather Control. Mr. Winthrop dies.

Now Vamp A cannot play superior Form of Mist to
continue the action, since he doesn't need the stealth.
